text:
[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved historical episodes where the tape looked like TSLA on 2026-09-18, the median realised 20-session return was 2.96%, with a mean of 2.39% and a standard deviation of 6.9%. The distribution is slightly left-skewed, meaning the downside tail is thicker than the upside, but 68% of the analogs finished above zero. The single number to anchor on for path risk is the median max adverse excursion of -3.53%, which shows that even the trades ending near the median had to survive a meaningful drawdown along the way.

[state]
The engine pulled these 50 analogs from 39 distinct sessions across 30 symbols because the current feature vector is defined by a specific combination of compressed short-term volatility against a volatile backdrop, thin dollar volume, and a sharp energy move. The most distinctive features are the 5d/20d volatility ratio at 0.489 (z-score -1.217), indicating recent price action has been unusually quiet relative to the past month, and the 20-session dollar-volume regime z-score at -1.558 (z-score -1.026), showing participation is well below normal. At the same time, 20-session realised volatility is elevated at 48.97% (z-score 0.983), and WTI crude changed 19.24% over 20 days (z-score 1.124). The name is also sitting -26.98% from its 52-week high (z-score -0.841) with a -14.35% drawdown from its 60-session peak (z-score -0.749). These features collectively weight the retrieval heavily toward the "name" group (30% weight) and the macro/market environment, pulling in names like TMO, SLB, LI, and AMZN that shared this mix of low relative volume, high absolute vol, and energy-driven macro stress. Only one prior TSLA session matched closely enough to enter the set.

[history]
Over the 20-session horizon, the 50 analogs produced returns ranging from -11.47% to 15.49%. The interquartile range spans from -1.25% (p25) to 6.87% (p75), while the p10 is -8.68% and the p90 is 10.51%. The skew is -0.288. In 18% of the episodes, the forward return fell below -5%, and in 4% it fell below -10%. None breached -20%. The worst outcome in the set belongs to LI (Li Auto ADR) on 2025-09-22, which returned -11.47% with a max adverse excursion of -13.16%. The best outcome was 15.49%. The closest match by distance was TMO (Thermo Fisher) on 2025-08-07 (distance 0.4262), which returned 8.33%. The only TSLA match occurred on 2025-08-07 (distance 0.4374), returning 8.87%. Other notable Consumer Disc. matches include NKE on 2023-10-10 (12.03%) and AMZN on 2016-12-14 (6.28%). The histogram shows the highest concentration of outcomes (10% share) in the 2.57% midpoint bin, with a visible secondary cluster of negative outcomes around the -8.66% and -1.92% midpoints.

[tails]
Endpoint returns understate the pain experienced during the 20 sessions. The median max adverse excursion across the analog set was -3.53%. At the p25, the worst intra-horizon drawdown was -7.38%, and at the p10 it was -10.99%. Looking at the probability of breaching specific drawdown thresholds at any point during the 20 sessions: 40% of the analogs breached a 5% drawdown, 14% breached a 10% drawdown, and 0% breached 15% or 20%. On the upside, the median max favourable excursion was 6.73%, reaching 9.45% at the p75 and 14.07% at the p90. This yields a historical reward/risk ratio of 1.91 based on excursions. The conformal interval, scaled to target 80% coverage, spans from -9.24% to 15.15% (width 24.38%), achieving an out-of-sample coverage of 87.4% on 2627 test queries.

[stress]
The baseline median is 2.39%. Several stress scenarios materially worsen that picture. The 2022 inflation / rate bear scenario produces a median forward return of -7.83% (delta -10.79% vs baseline), with a p10 of -15.46% and a 74% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; caveat: a nine-month window means the per-date cap of 2 analogs samples it repeatedly, so treat it as a regime description, not 50 independent events. The 2018-Q4 tightening scare yields a median of -6.29% (delta -9.25%), with a p10 of -12.52% and a 50% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; caveat: ended with a policy pivot in January 2019, which flatters the forward returns of late-window analogs. The 2020-02/03 liquidity crash gives a median of -3.2% (delta -6.16%), but the p10 plunges to -30.58% with a 72.9% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; caveat: central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns. The 2025-04 tariff shock results in a median of -0.86% (delta -3.82%), but a p10 of -12.15% and a 61.5% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; caveat: policy reversals inside the window make the tail asymmetric in a way specific to that episode. The Volatility spike (+2 sigma VIX) shock gives a median of -2.28% (delta -5.24%) with a p10 of -10.35%; caveat: VIX shocks mean-revert quickly, stressing entry timing more than terminal value. The Earnings release day shock yields a median of -1.18% (delta -4.14%) with a p10 of -13.93%; caveat: earnings dates for foreign private issuers come from 6-K full-text search and are noisier than 8-K Item 2.02 dates. The Crypto drawdown contagion shock gives a median of -1.99% (delta -4.95%) with a p10 of -14.13%; caveat: the BTC feature is a market-wide regime proxy, and any name-level linkage to crypto flows is not identified here. The Liquidity air pocket shock yields a median of 0.13% (delta -2.83%) but a p10 of -8.4%; caveat: gap20 is measured on the underlying exchange session, not a 7x24 venue, and for the tokenised wrapper verified on Bitget, 44.55% of realised hourly movement happened in closed hours. The 2024-08-05 carry unwind gives a median of -0.03% (delta -2.99%); caveat: reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, so H-day forward returns look benign even though intra-horizon excursion did not. The Policy-rate path re-pricing shock yields a median of -0.66% (delta -3.62%); caveat: uses DGS3MO/T10Y2Y levels as proxies, and transmission depends on duration and balance sheet not featured here. The FOMC decision day shock gives a median of 1.7% (delta -1.26%); caveat: only 92 decision days exist, so the analog set is small and highly overlapping. The China ADR de-rating shock yields a median of 1% (delta -1.96%); caveat: delisting and audit-access risks are structural and will not appear in a price/vol feature space. The 2023-03 regional bank stress actually improved the median to 3.07% (delta +0.11%); caveat: very short window, dominated by a handful of sessions. No scenarios were skipped.

[limits]
This analysis retrieves a historical conditional distribution; it does not forecast the future. The engine's own validation states explicitly: "Analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test. It is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source." The directional hit rate is 54%, and the matched coverage sharpness versus the same-name unconditional benchmark is -3.4%. The PIT chi-square is 363.9 against a critical value of 16.92. The retrieval found only 1 same-symbol match out of 50 analogs, meaning the distribution is built almost entirely on other names sharing similar feature states. The dataset spans 2016-09-20 to 2026-09-18 across 71 symbols. Regarding execution, the primary wrapper status is "measured" on the Bitget official MCP (TSLA/USDT perpetual). The reference cash market is shut for 81.4% of the week, and 44.55% of the wrapper's own realised hourly price movement landed in those closed hours. The tracking tier is "fair tracker" with a return correlation of 0.9637 and a tracking error of 98 bp/day. The basis band (p10 to p90) is -0.51% to 0.39%, and the spread is 0.26 bps. The wrapper caveat notes that a fair perpetual is not the underlying and not a redeemable spot token: at 98 bp/day of tracking error it carries idiosyncratic risk, funding applies, and the basis means the exit price can differ from the reference close the analog distribution is built on. For sizing reality, the closed-session return layer measured 6 weekend blocks. The median weekend block return was -0.312%, the p10 was -1.13%, and the standard deviation was 1.0081%. The median intra-weekend adverse excursion was -0.6715%, and 0% of the observed weekends breached the 5% drawdown threshold. These are wrapper returns measured while the reference market was shut and are NOT the retrieved outcome distribution above, which is built on 5x24 daily sessions of the underlying.
